title: ATLAS²
text:

Analysis Loolkit for Large Studies of Bisulfite-sequencing : ATLAS²


ATLAS² is a Nextflow-based pipeline for reproducible, scalable, and comprehensive analysis of bisulfite sequencing data. Designed for both newly generated and publicly available datasets, it performs extensive quality control, preprocessing, alignment, methylation calling, and exploratory analyses. With detailed reports and standardized outputs, ATLAS² delivers analysis-ready results that can be directly used for visualization, statistical modeling, and downstream epigenomic studies, from small experiments to large scale studies

title: References
text:
General parameters

outdir (default='./result' : string): A path to a directory where the pipeline results will be stored, i.e copied into from the work directory of each process using the directives of the configuration files for exact localization  workdir (default=null : string): A path to a directory where the pipeline will store every process instances, files as well as every conda environment, more details at Nextflow’s documentation  genome (default=null : string): A path to a folder containing a fasta file being the genome for alignment  samplesheet (default=null : string): A .csv file with studies accessions numbers and personalized input for metadata manipulation, for more details please refer to the test run at “First Launch of ATLAS²”  cpus (default=null : integer): An amount of CPUS available and allowed to the pipeline to use. memory: The amount of memory available and usable for the pipeline. The memory should be written in the form of X.MB,X.GB, X.TB, etc..  sub_samplesheet (default=null : string): A path to a file where each line should correspond to an accession number available from the metadata processed by the pipeline. Typically, this is used to filter samples out from larges studies  init (default=true : boolean) : A boolean that condition the execution of step from retrieving the metadata onwards. By default, init=true for the first run as we expect to first retrieve the metadata of our studies and explore the metadata to then plan out the analysis plan for each studies. It can be set to false afterwards or from the beginning in the case of self-curated data.  skip_preprocess (default=false : boolean) : A boolean allowing to skip all preprocessing step to start with alignment as the first step. PLACEHOLDER  bismark (default=true : boolean): Use Bismark Suite as the tools for alignment and post alignment processing, it is on by default. preprocess_only (default=false : boolean): Parameters to proceed apply only preprocessing step to the samples. run_single_end (default=false : boolean): Parameters to consider paired-end samples as if they were single ended and process them as such. For example, analysing sc-WGBS study would require this parameters.

title: References
text:
Process paramaters

metadata
path (default=null : string): Path to a metadata file (usually .csv). Typically after Initialization, i.e retrieving the metadata, if the metadata need some processing then it can be done externally and use the newly processed metadata as input using this paramater. 


fastqc
args (default=null : string): A string of arguments in the form of "--params1 --params2 ..." to give to this specific process as additional argument to the tool being used.


multiqc
args (default=null : string): A string of arguments in the form of "--params1 --params2 ..." to give to this specific process as additional argument to the tool being used. per_stage (default=null : string): Allow to create per condition report using multiqc by referencing a column from the metadata in the samplesheet. break_parent (default=null : string): Allow to give up seperating the input accession from the samplesheet into different report. For example, in case of two accession number as input to sample sheet both being GSE (large study) then instead of creating one report per GSE it will instad consider every sample as one unique study.


trimgalore
args (default=null : string): A string of arguments in the form of "--params1 --params2 ..." to give to this specific process as additional argument to the tool being used.

args (default=null : string): A string of arguments in the form of "--params1 --params2 ..." to give to this specific process as additional argument to the tool being used. skip (default=null : string): Allow to skip the genome preparation step and assume that it has already been done before. duplicate (default=null : string): Duplicate the genome folder with the alternative version to the output folder, i.e outdir.

title: How to launch the pipeline
text:
First, we will need to install conda (if not available) with the following command in a linux terminal
sudo apt install conda
Then using conda, we will create a new conda environment with Nextflow v25.10.4 (this version is the last one using the old parser in which the ATLAS² was coded)
cd path/to/where/you/want/the/environment/to/be ## optional but it's better to know where your environment will be created
conda create -p ./env -c conda-forge -c bioconda --override-channels nextflow=25.10.4

title: How to launch the pipeline
text:
Launch the pipeline

Now with the conda environment created, we will need to activate this environment
conda activate ./env/ #assuming you are in the correct directory, i.e the "path/to/where/you/want/the/environment/to/be" from before
After activating the conda environment, we can check if the right version of Nextflow is installed
nextflow -version
The following output should be printed
N E X T F L O W
      version 25.10.4 build 11173
      created XX-XX-XXXX XX:XX UTC (XX:XX CEST)
      cite doi:10.1038/nbt.3820
      http://nextflow.io
Now, you can theoretically launch any Nextflow pipeline using this conda environment, for example ATLAS², we can launch the pipeline with the following command
nextflow run main.nf 
But as you can see if you run the command above, we actually need to have the pipeline stored locally to be able to use main.nf, which contains the pipeline’s code.
 Future update might allow to skip this step entirely by directly launching the pipeline from a repository

title: How to launch the pipeline
text:
Retrieve the pipeline online

The pipeline can be found in this following public Github repository. You can clone this repository to have everything locally
## change your directory to where you want the pipeline to be stored
git clone https://github.com/ottarein/atlas-bis.git
Now, place yourself inside the pipeline directory you just cloned. From the root of that directory, running ls should show the following
modules nextflow.config params.yml ref_genome samplesheet.csv subworkflow
test-files, modules, ref_genome, subworkflow are folders while nextflow.config, params.yml, samplesheet.csv should be files.

title: Your First Launch of ATLAS²
text:
Parameters file
First, you will need a parameter file params.yml to make your life easier. A parameter file is a .yml file containing any parameters with their value that you would want to give to the pipeline. It substitute to simply adding them one by one in the command line after Nextflow run command
nextflow run main.nf -params-file params.yml
instead of
nextflow run main.nf --params1 value1 --params2 value2 ..
Here is an example of parameters file to use for now
outdir: './result'  
workdir: './work' 
samplesheet: "./samplesheet.csv"
sub_samplesheet: null
cpus: 4
memory: 16.GB

init: true
preprocess_only: true

title: Your First Launch of ATLAS²
text:
Samplesheet file
After creating your parameters file, you will need a samplesheet to tell the pipeline what are your samples’ accession number. A first samplesheet that we will be using is
accession,customs,extract,replace,stage
GSM9153248,,,,,
GSM9153249,,,,,
Those two WGBS sample from the paper Preventing CpG hypermethylation in oocytes safeguards mouse development.
A samplesheet is your way of telling the pipeline which samples you want to retrieve and how to identify them. A samplesheet has 5 columns : accession, customs, extract, replace and stage. For now we are only interested in the accession column. The samplesheet is only filled out with the accession number and you will run the pipeline with the argument init: true (by default) in your params.yml to do an Initialization step.

title: Welcome to ATLAS²
text:
ATLAS² (pronounced atlas-bis) is a powerful and reproducible Nextflow-based pipeline designed for comprehensive analysis of bisulfite sequencing data. Built to support both newly generated datasets and publicly available sequencing data, ATLAS² streamlines the entire processing workflow from raw reads to analysis-ready results.
Whether analyzing a single experiment or large-scale cohort studies involving hundreds of samples, ATLAS² provides a scalable and robust framework that ensures consistency, reproducibility, and ease of deployment across computing environments.
The pipeline performs extensive quality assessment at every stage of the analysis, generating detailed reports that allow users to evaluate sequencing quality, alignment performance, bisulfite conversion efficiency, coverage metrics, and methylation calling accuracy. Beyond quality control, ATLAS² includes a suite of preliminary analyses that help users rapidly explore their datasets and identify potential technical or biological patterns before conducting in-depth investigations.
All outputs are organized into standardized, analysis-ready formats, enabling seamless integration with downstream visualization tools, statistical frameworks, and custom bioinformatics workflows. By combining automation, comprehensive reporting, and scalability, ATLAS² empowers researchers to efficiently process and explore bisulfite sequencing datasets while maintaining full reproducibility and transparency.
From raw sequencing data to publication-ready analyses, ATLAS² provides a complete foundation for large-scale epigenomic studies.
